findings.title: Hardcoded Billing API Secret in Configuration File
findings.impact: An attacker with access to the configuration file (via repository, deployment logs, or process inspection) obtains the billing API credentials. This allows unauthorized access to the billing system and potential fraudulent transactions.

findings.title: Arbitrary Command Injection via Model Output
findings.impact: The function 'summarize_and_run' executes arbitrary shell commands derived from model output with shell=True, allowing Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the operator's machine.

findings.title: Missing Authorization Scoping in run_tool() Function
findings.impact: The run_tool() function allows the model to execute refunds on ANY account without verifying authorization. A customer can manipulate the model into issuing unauthorized refunds to attacker accounts.

findings.title: Race Condition and Data Loss in Memory Persistence
findings.impact: Non-atomic read-modify-write pattern on the memory JSON file causes concurrent writes to lose data. In a service with multiple concurrent conversations, memory updates can be overwritten and lost.

findings.title: JSON Corruption via Unescaped Model Output
findings.impact: The remember_from_reply() function appends model output to JSON without explicit validation. While json.dumps() does escape, lack of post-write validation is a weakness.

findings.title: Prompt Injection via Untrusted Retrieval Context
findings.impact: Customer-provided ticket content is added directly to the retrieval index without sanitization. An attacker can craft a malicious ticket that overrides the system prompt and manipulates the model into unauthorized tool execution.
